context_data.content: ## · And mitigating AI risks is a true challenge in business adoption Hallucination, bias, confidentiality: these are the risks and limits that are holding companies back from using AI, through a healthy respect for both the regulatory framework, and a context where the acceptable margin of error in decision-making is low. So what do we mean by this? · Hallucination: generative Als are based on a multitude of documents. When the next word to predict matches the truth, all is well. But otherwise? They must choose one option, and can hallucinate untruths with great aplomb. Users therefore need to be trained to use these AIs properly, and to verify every single claim they make. . Bias: they are rarely intentional, but algorithmic biases are based on data reflecting human practice. The system can therefore discriminate against a specific group of people. A major obstacle for businesses is to identify potential biases (lack of qualified data), raise awareness among employees and have the resources to do so (a dedicated inclusive team, for instance, or a taxonomy programmed with contextual information), and then deal with the biases. . Privacy: The confidentiality rules of GenAl, and ChatGPT in particular, are still poorly understood. Bear in mind that any data and/or code sent to one of these platforms is likely to be used for subsequent training, which raises issues of confidentiality of corporate data (or that of its customers) and intellectual property. Overcoming these risks is not an option, it's a sine qua non condition for some businesses. However, the adoption of AI itself is facilitated when it is designed responsibly from the outset: ethical standards reinforce confidence in its use; responsible practices in critical sectors such as human resources guarantee a positive and equitable societal impact; operational excellence prevents abuse and ensures that the AI is beneficial and reliable... Adopting a responsible AI is thus becoming a crucial approach to minimizing risk. ## . Key Issue ### How do we turn this AI revolution into a competitive advantage? We need new "software" to tackle this profound change in the way we work, and even in the way we do business. New responsible governance must overcome all the risks generated by the use of AI and generative AI. By evolving into an "AI-ready" business, organizations put in place the conditions that will enable them to meet the key business challenges of the future, and perpetuate their business practices and even their business model. It's a moment of truth for organizations: yes, there is a turning point ahead; yet it does not have to be a problem: by implementing a "responsible-by-design" approach, organizations are better equipped to deal with the risks -not just compliance risks, but also business risks- created by the exploding use of Al (see pillars). Ekimetrics intends to accompany this revolution with a simple, easy-to-understand framework to support these organizations in their AI transformation and the use of these technologies. We have therefore developed 7 pillars of responsible AI, designed to create this competitive edge (see next chapter). ## · Empower business with AI and GenAI solutions through responsible governance Anticipate future regulations, limit the risk of damage to image and reputation, improve the efficiency, accuracy and durability of models, all while generating value: to meet all these challenges, Ekimetrics has developed 7 pillars of responsible governance, which can be considered true operational and business tools. THE 7 PILLARS OF RESPONSIBLE AI AND THEIR BUSINESS ADVANTAGES 1. Security Ensure the security of personal and sensitive data. GDPR compliance. Data Clean Rooms: value of personal data. 2. Transparency Communicate intentions clearly regarding data and models. Improve trustworthiness and product adoption. Model cards are important for documentation, transmission, and reuse. Registries are probably needed for the AI Act. 3. Interpretability Provide access to the factors that influenced the decision/prediction. More control, easier to debug. Allows explainability. Required for some products in the AI Act. 4. Explainability Explain the predictions provided by the models, work on the user interfaces. Improve adoption/trust. Human agency. 5. Vigilance Avoid possible prejudice to the users' interests, exclude discriminatory biases. Scandal prevention. AI Act compliance. Potential new customers. 6. Robustness Measure and ensure performance and stability throughout the system lifecycle. Performance. Control. 7. Sustainability Limit the system's energy consumption and carbon footprint. Financial gains, simplicity, control, acceleration. ### TYPES OF SECURITY AI FAILURE: - DATA BREACH OR LEAKAGE - NON-COMPLIANCE - RANSOMWARE / MALWARE - PHISHING - FAKE NEWS - MODEL AND DATA POISONING ### WHO'S IN CHARGE? EXCOM DPO COMPLIANCE/LEGAL IT MANAGEMENT DATA TEAMS FINAL USERS

## CUSTOMER STORIES: CRAFTING EXPLAINABLE SOLUTIONS FOR ENHANCED ADOPTION THROUGH USER-CENTRIC APPROACHES

· Challenge: We build all our solutions with explainability by design. For users, to understand where the recommendations of the algorithms are coming from is key for trust and adoption. For example, we have two customers from very different industries (food and publishing) both wanting a solution displaying the performance of their point of sales on interactive maps.

. Approach: Different types of users, from different businesses, need different types of information. User experience interviews are essential to understand their specific needs, and frequent user tests during the development allow the interface to be tweaked to be as relevant as possible.

. Outcome: The interfaces produced for both clients were very different, addressing the specific needs of each, increasing user satisfaction and adoption rates. This method establishes a foundation of trust through customized interfaces, that is adapted to diverse user needs.

## 5· Vigilance pillar

### Core concept

Avoid prejudice to the users' interests, in particular discriminatory biases and addictive processes

### What are the risks?

· For your end customers > Discrimination based on gender, age, skin color, nationality, sexual orientation, etc.

· For your organization > brand image/reputation, ethics and compliance issues, loss of customers

Where do you start?

V Building inclusive/diverse development teams

V Creation of checklists to standardize bias checks*

V Add algorithmic layers to verify the absence of bias, particularly in the selection

of input data and output predictions

V Bias correction/mitigation

### What's the competitive advantage?

· For your end customers > trust

· For your business customers > service satisfaction, development of new marketing or sales strategies

(= a properly identified bias can be used to target new categories of people, products or services in the market, which would have previously been excluded. See business case below)

· For your organization > compliance, respect for fairness

### *BIAS CONTROL: 9 QUESTIONS BEFORE PROCEEDING

- Does my dataset contain personal data?

- If so, are you GDPR compliant?

- Is the data pseudo-anonymized?

- Does my dataset contain populations at risk of discrimination?

- Can my solution have a strong impact on my users?

- Have I tested for potential discrimination?

- Is my dataset balanced?

- Is there a risk of bias in the way the data was collected?

- Do I have a diverse team of data scientists?

## CUSTOMER STORIES: BREAKING GENDER BIAS IN TARGETED MARKETING FOR A CAR MANUFACTURER

. Challenge: A car manufacturer scoring their client base to target those with a high probability of buying a second car, were concerned that the model was biased in favor of men.

. Approach: We performed a bias measurement and observed that women had a lower probability of being targeted. This bias limited outreach to a significant portion of the customer base and resulted in missed opportunities.

. Outcome: We mitigated the bias without lowering the model's performance and increased the potential client base.

## DATA AND MODEL DRIFTS

- Data drift refers to the phenomenon where the characteristics of the input data that an AI model was trained on, gradually diverge from the characteristics of the data it encounters in a real-world production environment. This can occur due to changes in user behavior, shifts in market trends, or other external factors that influence data distribution over time.

- Model drift refers to the situation where an AI model's performance gradually diminishes over time as the underlying assumptions or conditions in the operational environment change. This can occur due to shifts in user preferences, alterations in the business landscape, or other dynamic factors that impact the relevance of the model.

## CUSTOMER STORIES: UNLEASHING THE POWER OF MMM THROUGH PROACTIVE MONITORING AND RETRAINING

· Challenge: Putting Mixed Marketing Models (MMM) in production provides the ability to make near real-time adjustments, leading to a more agile and adaptive marketing strategy. However, the performance of the models can decrease over time with market changes.

. Approach: Monitoring and retraining are integral components of mixed marketing models in production. Monitoring ensures that the models produce accurate predictions, while retraining upholds the models' effectiveness over time, adapting to evolving market dynamics.

. Outcome: Together, monitoring and retraining establish a robust feedback loop. This iterative cycle is paramount in preserving the models' effectiveness.

<!-- PageFooter: page 15 -->
<!-- PageBreak -->

## 7· Sustainability pillar

### Core concept

Limit energy consumption and reduce the system's carbon footprint (= reducing the impact of AI itself)

### What are the risks?

· For all > pollution, carbon-based electricity production, contribution to global warming

· For your organization > increase IT's contribution to your organization's carbon footprint, brand image/reputation

Where do you start?

V Measure the carbon footprint of your Al projects to identify potential savings

- By creating dedicated governance and a carbon footprint tracking table

- Install consumption trackers (=free software in open-source libraries such as CodeCarbon) that monitor energy and the impact of electricity consumption

V Reduce consumption

- By using simpler, more frugal models

- Implement good consumer practices.

Example: close clusters on the cloud or your servers.

### What's the competitive advantage?

· For all > improved carbon footprint

· For your business customers > simplification of systems, easier to check and debug, improved interpretability and vigilance

· For your organization > lower energy costs, reduced CO2 emissions

So, training data collected during this period likely captured more content reflecting the prevalence of sexual harassment and violence against women.353 Either way, the biases and blindspots of society are scraped into databases for training Al models, and those models conjure up their outputs based on what they have in those databases.

Another problem with datasets used to train large language models can be that they lack representation of languages from groups that are already disproportionately marginalized or excluded. Over 60% of all websites, for instance, are in English. As a result, large language models underperform in non-English languages, resulting in disparities in content for different groups in a global society. Training the same algorithm on datasets of Korean or French texts, for instance, would certainly result in different model outputs. Moreover, large language models may harbor hidden biases based on language. Recent research revealed that certain Al systems exhibit a higher likelihood of recommending the death penalty for a fictional defendant who presents a statement in African American English (AAE)-a dialect spoken by millions in the United States-compared to a statement in Standardized American English (SAE).354 Additionally, the chatbots were more prone to assigning AAE speakers to less prestigious jobs.

The issue of bias is not limited to text-based Al but can also be seen in image-based models. Some synthetic image generation systems overrepresent white skin tones and male features.355 For instance, when researchers evaluated images created by Stable Diffusion against statistics for US demographics for various occupations, they found discrepancies: Although statistics showed that women constitute 39% of doctors, images of women as doctors accounted for only 7% of the images of doctors generated by the Al model. The study established a similar pattern for judges: Women represent 34% of the profession but appear in just 3% of the images of judges.356 More broadly, outputs from generative Al might reflect this pattern of discrimination toward other specific social and religious groups.357

Efforts to correct these trends can lead to imbalances, too. ## 1. Security pillar

### Core concept

Ensure the protection and control of your customers' or users' personal data and your organization's sensitive data.

What are the risks?

· For your end customers > disclosure and misuse

of their data, possibly damaging to their image

· For your organization > brand image/reputation and business, industrial espionage, sabotage, ethics and compliance issues, GDPR fines

Where do you start? If you use a public tool like ChatGPT:

V Do not provide information protected by intellectual property rights

If you have concerns about GAFAM technologies:

v Customize your own open-source GenAl

Personal data

## · Generative AI for dummies

### Generative AIs create content...

... as if they were you, based on one of your requests. Text, images, video, sound: they magnify human creative processes; it only takes them a few seconds to generate a text (with ChatGPT3) or an image (with Midjourney).

### What is the difference with the "old" AI?

Until now, AIs were based mainly on "structured" data: descriptive, numerical information in spreadsheets (business accounts, temperature measurements for weather forecasts, sales figures, etc.). Generative AIs are based on "unstructured" data (text, images, video, sound); in a way, they create "new" content.

### What challenges to achieve what success?

### Relevance.

How do we control hallucinations and biases while respecting the regulatory framework, in a context with a low acceptable error on decision-making? How do we ensure that the content is contextualized and actionable in a specific sector, business, use and time?

<!-- PageFooter: 3 3 GPT-3 and GPT-4 are LLMs (Large Language Models), which are generative AI algorithms, a Deep Learning method, a subset of Machine Learning, itself a subset of Data Science. page 03 -->
<!-- PageBreak -->

<!-- PageHeader: Ekimetrics. -->

Generative AI's true significance lies in its capacity to address specific problems within well-structured ecosystems. Beyond the hype, it becomes a valuable tool when applying meticulous data preprocessing and interface development to deliver human-readable results, through techniques like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) (a technique incorporating the corrections made by annotators to a ranking of answers proposed by the generative AI algorithm. Thanks to RLHF, the algorithm learns to generate responses that would be validated by humans).

>> From a business viewpoint, the goal is to overcome the current pitfalls of AI and LLMs to deliver trustworthy models that exactly and specifically match an organization's strategy and operations.

### Embedding.

How do we embed these complex models in specific IT legacy and activation tools? How can we be sure they match an organization and its processes? How do we combine them with lighter models and human-led decision-making steps?

Integrating Generative AI into an ecosystem mirrors traditional data projects, involving data structuring and user-centric refinement. Its unique strength lies in presenting meaningful outcomes to users, through constant adaptation and incorporation of feedback to enhance its accuracy.

>> In practice, AI needs to be fully integrated and embedded in a company's workflows, processes and systems.

### Control.

How do we control the cost of internalizing such technologies? Beyond the tech component and the training cost, what technical skills are required? How can we trust the security and privacy of these technologies?

Monitoring Generative AI in production poses distinctive challenges compared to traditional algorithms. User feedback and comparisons become pivotal in defining a good model and ensuring long-term effectiveness while mitigating bias. Maintenance efforts are vital to uphold performance quality, and users will play an essential role in adapting to and refining their interactions with Generative AI.

>> Securing access to data requires deploying Responsible AI models by design, compliant with the EU AI Act and developed with weighted models to control for cost and energy consumption.

<!-- PageFooter: page 04 -->
<!-- PageBreak -->

<!-- PageHeader: Ekimetrics. -->

## · Responsible AI for dummies

### The issue of impact.

Previously, Al was often a matter for specialists - data, sales, marketing, IT, etc. Today, although not everyone works with Machine Learning, anyone can use ChatGPT. In fact, it took this technology just 5 days to pass the million-user mark, and two months to reach 100,000 million.

This democratization of AI use therefore represents a major turning point: HR, the justice system, public services, etc .: all spheres of society now benefit from it -sometimes with proven and critical societal impacts (see diagram). This democratization requires increased attention to excellence in AI implementation, with stronger monitoring and equal rights protection. Safeguards must therefore be implemented from both a technical and a human standpoint, taking risks into account and correcting them as best we can.

## WHAT ARE BIASES AND WHY ARE THEY DANGEROUS?

Social bias broadly encompasses disparate treatment or outcomes between social groups, arising from historical and structural power asymmetries. In the context of Natural Language Processing (NLP), this entails representational harms (misrepresentation, stereotyping, unequal system performance, derogatory language, and exclusionary norms) and allocative harms (direct discrimination and indirect discrimination).

Discrimination is the unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of ethnicity, age, sex, or disability.

A protected attribute is the shared identity trait that determines the group identity of a social group (gender, age, ethnicity, etc.).

<!-- PageFooter: page 05 -->
<!-- PageBreak -->

<!-- PageHeader: Ekimetrics. -->

context_data.content:
## Les recommandations de Data For Good pour les utilisateurs

Rester vigilant et questionner les réponses données par les ChatBot des entreprises/administrations. Notamment vérifier lesquelles sont entièrement algorithmiques et lesquelles pourraient reposer sur des données personnelles et créer des biais. En cas de soupçon de biais, ne pas hésiter à saisir l'autorité compétente (CNIL, Autorité de la Concurrence).

### Biais inhérents au modèle

La deuxième composante fondamentale de la fabrication du biais est évidemment le modèle en lui-même.

Les modèles d'IA générative ne discriminent pas volontairement, ni utilisent directement les variables « sensibles » telles que origine ethnique, genre, âge, situation de handicap, .... Pourtant, les biais persistent, car il ne suffit pas de supprimer les variables sensibles pour faire disparaître les biais : ils apparaissent au travers des variables dites « proxys ». Il s'agit de variables en apparence inoffensives, mais qui sont corrélées aux variables sensibles et portent donc la représentation du biais (le code postal du lieu de résidence est par exemple un bon proxy de l'origine ethnique).

À noter que c'est parce que le modèle fonde sa décision sur les proxys que les enquêtes de testing, qui consistent à tester l'algorithme avec des données qui ne varient que de la variable à tester (par exemple deux CV identiques dont seul le genre va changer) ne détectent souvent pas la discrimination [118].

Il existe plusieurs façons d'agir sur le modèle pour atténuer l'apparition de biais algorithmiques. Une des solutions envisageables est de forcer une discrimination positive. Dans le cas de DALL-E, le choix a été fait de rajouter des mots aux prompts envoyés pour faire apparaître plus de femmes et de personnes de couleur [119]. Des internautes s'en sont aperçus en tronquant leur demande : « génère moi une personne tenant une pancarte où il est écrit ». Au milieu des propositions inintelligibles se distinguent des images sur lesquelles on peut lire « black » ou « female », suggérant que ces mots ont été ajoutés au prompt afin de faire remonter des images plus diverses.

<!-- PageFooter: [118] https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/discrimination-algorithmique-des-syst%C3%A8me-dia-mesurer- d%C3%A9tecter-besse/ [119] https://www.newscientist.com/article/2329690-ai-art-tool-dall-e-2-adds-black-or-female-to-some- image-prompts/ Biais algorithmiques de l'IA générative 69 -->
<!-- PageBreak -->

Created with DALL-E, an AI system by OpenAI

Created with DALL-E, an AI system by OpenAI

Réponses choisies [120] d'images générées par DALL-E au prompt «a person wearing a shirt that says», juillet 2022.

Mais la discrimination positive n'est pas la seule approche - elle n'est même généralement pas considérée comme viable par la communauté scientifique. Des solutions techniques existent ou émergent, de la contrainte d'équilibre des taux d'erreurs [121] à l'utilisation du transport optimal de Lipschitz [122].

## Performance et validation du résultat

Une part importante du processus de création d'une intelligence artificielle, est de valider qu'elle fonctionne, en testant ses performances. Une méthode classique d'évaluation de la performance d'un modèle d'IA est le calcul du F-score, qui recherche un équilibre entre la précision (la part de réponses « justes » obtenues par le modèle) et le rappel (la part de réponses justes que le modèle a manqué).

Ce type de calcul de la performance pose un problème de taille : la réponse du modèle sur la population sur-représentée dans ses données d'apprentissage prend une proportion bien plus importante que celle des populations minoritaires. Et lorsqu'un modèle se trompe rarement sur la majorité mais est systématiquement moins bon envers une minorité, son F-score reste bon malgré la discrimination que le modèle apprend.

Des nouveaux critères de performance tenant compte du risque de biais algorithmique ont été définis afin d'anticiper les différents types de discrimination algorithmique. Mais ces différentes métriques sont encore trop peu utilisées et peuvent s'avérer compliquées à mettre en place, par manque d'accès direct à la variable sensible (origine ethnique, genre, âge ... ).

\* [12] https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/discrimination-algorithmique-des-syst%C3%A8me-dia-mesurer- d%C3%A9tecter-besse/

[122] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.14063.pdf

Les biais ethniques ont marqué l'histoire des biais algorithmiques avec des exemples fondateurs, de la justice algorithmique (83), plus sévère à l'encontre des prévenus de couleur, en passant par les solutions de santé diminuant l'accès aux soins de certaines populations (84), jusqu' au concours de beauté [85] perpétuant les standards de beauté caucasiens[86]. Les IA génératives n'échappe malheureusement pas aux biais algorithmiques.

Les milieux militants le savent [87] : la représentation est clé pour s'affranchir des stéréotypes. Dans sa conférence TED de 2010, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie [88] nous mettait en garde contre l'unicité des représentations qui renforce les stéréotypes. Or si l'on considère que les contenus de demain seront massivement produits à partir d'intelligence artificielle generative, les biais ethniques de ces IA vont continuer d'enfermer des populations dans des stéréotypes racistes. Pour une intelligence artificielle, un PDG est par défaut un homme blanc. Dans les premières versions de DALL-E, vous n'obteniez pas de personne de couleur à moins d'en faire la demande spécifique. Nous verrons plus bas que pour tenter de masquer ce biais, DALL-E rajoute la demande spécifique dans les prompts de son interface grand public. Si en 2023 les résultats sont moins stéréotypes qu'en 2022, l'algorithme, lui, n'en semble pas moins fondamentalement biaisé.

Prompt: ceo; Date: April 6, 2022

Réponses à des prompts simples de DALL-E, 2022 [89]

L'intelligence artificielle associe également certains adjectifs aux personnes de couleur. Demandez un homme, vous aurez des images d'hommes blanc. Un « homme en colère » fera apparaître des hommes de couleur et « un homme assis sur le sol d'une prison » ne sera presque jamais caucasien [90]. Il en va de même dans la génération de texte. Dans les histoires générées par chatGPT [91] les protagonistes sont blancs, les princesses sont blondes ...

Outre les problématiques de représentation et de véhiculation de stéréotypes qui font reculer des combats menés pour la diversité, L'IA générative peut alimenter des

\* [85] https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/sep/08/artificial intelligence-beauty-contest- doesnt-like-black-people

\* [86] https://www.npr.org/sections/codeswitch/2019/02/06/685506578/is-beauty-in-the-eyes-of-the-colonizer

\* [87] https://www.mondefemmes.org/produit/genre-et-communication-decrypter-les-medias/

\* [88] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D9Ihs241zeg

\* [89] https://www.vice.com/en/article/wxdawn/the-ai-that-draws-what-you-type-is-very-racist-shocking- no-one

\* [91] https://medium.com/geekculture/write-a-novel-using-ai-openai-chatgpt-c02be59cd937

haines raciales et encourager des actions violentes. En une journée seulement, des individus malveillants ont réussi à dévoyer Tay, le chatbot de Microsoft déployé en 2016 sur Twitter, qui en est venue à souhaiter la mort des féministes et à accuser les Juifs d'être responsables des attentats du 11 septembre [921.

En 2020, Timnit Gebru, alors co-directrice de l'IA éthique chez Google, signe un article qui lui vaudra son éviction [93]. Dans cet article, elle dénonce les dangers des perroquets stochastiques [94] - ces modèles de langages tels que chatGPT qui associent des mots en fonction de ce qui a été observé dans un corpus d'apprentissage. Si les textes d'apprentissage contiennent un langage biaisé ou des stéréotypes, alors les modèles d'intelligence artificielle vont les répéter, et souvent les aggraver, dans leur génération de texte.

Après l'image et le texte, les IA génératrices de musique ne sont pas en reste : en 2020 le rappeur virtuel FN Meka [95], une intelligence artificielle aux 10 millions d'abonnés sur Tik Tok, signe avec le label Capitol Records. Quelques jours plus tard le contrat est rompu : FN Meka crée du contenu toujours plus toxique et violent, qui véhicule des stéréotypes racistes.
